newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power holds in sluggish trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power holds in sluggish trading.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady again on Tuesday in sparse trading, stalled by mild weather in the region and transmission constraints, industry sources said.
Next-day peak prices for non-firm deliveries in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) were in the $16.50-17.25 per Megawatt hour (MWh) range, sources said, unchanged from Monday's levels.
Similar prices were discussed for the remainder of October despite expectations for colder temperatures by week's end in the Midwest.
In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Wednesday delivery were mostly stable at $16.00 early and then offered late at $15.50.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was in the $12.50-14.00 area, up from Monday's trading between $10.00 and $12.00.
November ECAR prices were talked in the $17.50 area, while the December market remained around $19.00. January/February 1997 business was discussed slightly stronger in the $21.00 area.
Peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) were talked steady again in the $14.50-15.00 range.
Off-peak, non-firm MAPP electricity prices were also flat in the $10.25-10.50 range.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in the northern part of the region was in the $17.00-19.00 area, while prices in the southern part were higher in the $23.00-24.00 range due to stronger natural gas prices.
Off-peak prices in SPP remained in the $12.50-14.00 area.
December SPP prices were talked in the $22.10-22.40 range, while the January SPP market hovered in the $21.25-22.35 area.
SPP prices for the first and second quarters of 1997 were equally flat in the $20.65-20.85 and $21.00 areas, respectively.

Separately, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in Arizona is likely to be back to full power by late Tuesday, Arizona Public Service Co, the plant's operator, reported earlier today.

Also reported early Tuesday, TVA Nuclear's 1,148 MW Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Soddy Daisy, Tenn., which was shut Friday due to a leak on a reactor coolant pump's seal, is expected to restart later today.
